- Relevant family medical history: Mother has migraines.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (initial): Migraine-type headache with features compatible with migraine with aura (photophobia, visual phenomena, unilateral emphasis around the right eye, episodic pattern with partial NSAID relief). Plan to perform a full neurological examination and ophthalmoscopic (fundoscopy) assessment to exclude red flags.
- Differential diagnoses considered (aligned with DDx and transcript):
  - Migraine with aura (high likelihood): Supported by photophobia, visual disturbances, recent new-onset disabling headache, family history of migraines, partial response to NSAIDs, and absence of systemic/infectious signs.
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) related to estrogen-containing oral contraceptive (medium likelihood): New, persistent headache in a patient on OCP; risk factor present; imaging needed to exclude.
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) (medium likelihood): Young woman with headaches and visual symptoms; would assess with fundoscopy for papilledema; obesity not described.
  - Intracranial mass / raised intracranial pressure (low likelihood): Persistent headache since onset; morning predominance could raise suspicion but less likely given short 3-day course without focal deficits.
  - Meningitis/encephalitis (low likelihood): Photophobia present but absence of fever, neck stiffness, or altered mental status makes infection unlikely.
- Management priorities:
  - Schedule urgent/early neurology exam with fundoscopy to assess for papilledema and red flags.
  - Consider trial of analgesia tailored to migraines: stronger NSAID alternative plus paracetamol, to be taken with food.
  - Reassess need to modify or review hormonal contraception given migrainous features with photophobia; plan to check blood pressure at examination to assess safety of continued OCP.
  - Provide patient education: seek urgent care if headaches worsen, new neurologic symptoms develop, fever, neck stiffness, or confusion; A&E visit if red flags arise.
- Plan details (to be implemented):
  - Book appointment with clinic support for a full examination including neurological assessment and fundoscopy.
  - Start medication plan: stronger NSAID alternative in addition to paracetamol; take with food.
  - Monitor for escalation in symptoms; reassess if headaches change or worsen.
  - Consider pharmacologic contraception reassessment based on migraine features; blood pressure will be checked during the upcoming examination to determine suitability of the current pill.
  - If symptoms are unbearable or rapidly progressive before the exam, advised to go to A&E for evaluation.

  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Photophobia, visual disturbances (flashes/light), new severe headache with functional impact, family history of migraines, partial NSAID response; absence of systemic signs
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) related to estrogen-containing oral contraceptive
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: New, persistent headache in a patient on combined OCP; risk factor for CVST; needs imaging to exclude
- Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri)
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Young to middle-aged woman with headaches and visual symptoms; would require fundoscopy for papilledema; no obesity noted
